questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I decided to go to Milan because i would love to go to Italy, i also wanted to go to a place where I could get the erasmus scolarship, and finally I only speach Danish and English so it is nice that you can take masters courses in University of Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay the puplic transportantion system is nice.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult there are a lot of different buildings and rooms and you need an app to find them for each course. there are people that you can ask in most buildings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We used spotahome, its good to do this many months before you have to move there. It is in general pretty expencive to live in Milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to to find out where you will be taking the courses and find a flat close to there because Milan is a very big city, I lived not to fr from the center but still had 50 min transport to citta studi. It is also nice to know that living in the center of Milan is not essential as the city is big and there are nice neighborhoods in a large parameter especially to the north and east.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We ended up living three people in a two person flat for it to be affordable. I herd of a lot of scams so be carefull.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It took a long time to get my OLA approved

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We sent and application, through the website i think and then we sent our online learning agrement to the person we were assigned, this was in some pdf file that was a bit har to find.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Massimo Costa is always helpful but can be a bit slow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me it went pretty well I got maybe 4/5 courses that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a bit of a puzzle to find a combination of courses that dont overlap and dont have large breaks in the middle of the day. Because of that i would recommend to get a lot of preaprovals because the sceduals of each course is not available before august/september.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses are very theoretical, not a lot of praactical lab work and not a lot of reading. The courses were relavant and interesting but having 5 at the same time made it a bit difficult.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mostly took first semester master courses, which i would recommend. I think the level was fitting, some courses were a bit difficult if they were to far from my background.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot less reading, less lab, less exersices, so in general a lot less practical teaching. This was nice because it gave a lot of free time but if you are there mostly for educational reasons its maybe not the best. It is very lecture based and the exams are based on learning things by heart.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MOLECULAR PHARMACOLOGY AND IMMUNOLOGY (F9Y09-)
RATIONAL DESIGN AND STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF BIOACTIVE MOLECULES (F1B0F-)
FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS (F9Y0F-)
BIO-BASED INNOVATION IN FOOD INDUSTRY (G640G-)
DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY AND GENETICS (F9Y02-)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the functional genomics course because it was very usefull and the professor is really good. I would also recommend the molecular immunology and pharmacology as it was a realy interesting course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffe is very cheap, groceries were a bit more expencive than expected. The under 26 monthly travel card made transportsation very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think they hosted a ski trip.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to cities close by like Lecco or Bergamo for day trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to eat and have cheap coffe and aperativo in the sun! Museums are a bit expensive but some are worth it also go to the top of the duomo on a clear day it is turisty but beautyful. Also it is so nice to take weekend trips to other italian cities like Rome or Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe take more courses from the same master so you have more oppertunities to talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It can feel a bit unsafe especially at night, because there is a bigger catcalling culture and the subway stops running after midnight and the buses after this are a bit sketchy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the food and that the people of all ages are on the streets with there freinds enyoing life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will have a lot of courses at a time. The teaching is very theoretical. The city and culture is amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is nice to check the exam form. Ones with a precentation as exam are nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seing a new culture and getting to know the traditions and a bit of the language, and meeting a lot of nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting all the preperations to add up, to have enough courses that fit and getting a scedual that works and getting everything approved. ALso the exam period was very though i had 5 exams in a weak because many of my subjects were split into two sepperate exams even though they were only 6 ECTS, so in total i had 8 exams that were nearly all written with pretty high expectations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
